_comment: The front door's own completeness registry -- read by Test-PracticeClaims.ps1 check H.
WHAT THIS EXISTS FOR. The repository README carries a section enumerating everything under
tools/. It was complete on the day it was written and went incomplete as units were added: the
table described seven units against thirteen entries on disk, and the newest of the three it
had never mentioned was the only one that makes any of the practice actually fire. Nothing in
this repository went red for that, because an enumeration-by-example rots in the one direction
no check here was looking: everything it DOES name still resolves, so every citation passed,
every section was sourced, every figure was dated, and the omission was invisible from inside a
green run. That is the third time this defect class has had to be fixed here -- a remembered
list of shipped scripts that said six when it was nine, and a whitelisted pin sweep that
exempted whatever nobody remembered to add, are the other two.
SO IT IS CHECKED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, like every other registry in this directory. Forward: an
entry on disk that the section does not name is undocumented. Reverse: a unit the section names
that is not on disk is stale -- and that half is the quieter one, because a row pointing at a
directory somebody renamed reads exactly like a row pointing at one that is still there.
WHY THE CHECK LIVES IN THE tools/ GATE AND READS OUTSIDE IT. The front door is at the
repository root, which is outside this gate's subject -- and the README says so about itself in
two places, having gone stale before. Reaching out is not a new liberty: the negative-claim
inversion already reads planning documents that could never live under a redaction scan, and
its scope is a registry rather than a tree walk. This is the same shape, with the same cost --
a root that does not hold the front door cannot answer the question -- and the same remedy,
which is the marker below.
repository_marker -- HOW THE CHECK KNOWS IT IS LOOKING AT THE RIGHT FRONT DOOR, and why it is
not the section heading. A distribution carries a README.md at its root too, and it is a
DIFFERENT DOCUMENT: the pack's front door is authored under one name and takes the
recipient-facing name on the way in, precisely because the repository already has a README.md.
So a check that keyed on 'is there a README.md here' would read the pack's front door, fail to
find a section that was never in it, and report the pack broken. It keys on the SOURCE name
instead, which the builder asserts is nowhere on disk in a built pack -- present means this
tree is the repository the front door belongs to, absent means it is not, and the check reports
SKIPPED rather than FAIL or PASS. Registered as a bundle boundary in share-pack.json, so the
day a distribution starts carrying the section that entry fails as stale.
The marker is deliberately NOT the section heading. Keying on the heading would make a mangled
or deleted heading indistinguishable from a distribution -- the exact fail-open this check is
here to close -- so a missing heading in a tree that HAS the marker is a FAIL with the heading
quoted, and an empty unit list refuses outright.
worked_example / counter_example -- POSITIVE AND NEGATIVE CONTROLS ASSERTED ON EVERY RUN, not
only in the self-test, for the reason every pattern table in this directory carries its own
example: a comparison that has stopped matching produces an empty finding set, and an empty
finding set is what a complete section produces. The worked example is the unit whose omission
is the reason this check exists, so a run in which it is not both on disk and named in the
section is a run whose PASS means nothing.
The counter-example is a near-miss chosen where a near-miss MATTERS: it is a real unit's name
with one token appended, so it resolves against nothing under an exact comparison and resolves
against its shorter sibling under a prefix-wise one. A stale row satisfied by a real directory
that merely starts the same way is the failure it forbids, and the check refuses a
counter-example that is not an extension of some entry on disk -- absence proves nothing about
exactness unless the name was a candidate for the loose comparison in the first place.
exempt -- AN ENTRY UNDER tools/ THAT DELIBERATELY IS NOT LISTED IN THE SECTION. IT IS EMPTY,
AND THAT IS THE POINT OF HAVING IT: the alternative to registering a decision is a silence, and
a silence is what let three units go unmentioned in the first place. Each entry needs the
reason, and it is checked in both directions too -- an exemption naming something that is not
on disk has outlived its file, and an exemption for something the section names anyway covers
nothing. Either way it fails as stale rather than sitting there suppressing forever.

worked_example.reason: The unit this check was written for. It is the newest, it is the only one that installs anything rather than being read, and it was the omission that mattered: a reader of the front door had no way to learn that the firing layer existed. If it is ever absent from disk or from the section, this check has stopped measuring the thing it was built to measure.

counter_example.reason: The worked example's name with a plausible suffix -- and every other unit here is spelled '<something>-toolkit', so this is the name a reader guesses rather than an invented string. It must resolve against nothing: under an exact comparison it does not, and under a prefix-wise or -like comparison it would be satisfied by claude-practice-layer, which is how a stale row survives a completeness check. Asserted to be an extension of a real entry as well, since a counter-example that was never a candidate for the loose match proves nothing by failing to match.
